ports.note: Every layer port, on every map, whatever its parameters say. The ports used to vary with an inputMode parameter -- reasoningInput, rasterInput, polygonInput, networkInput were four separate declarations of that -- so the port a connection needed might not exist on the node. Which renderer draws is now read from what is wired: src/core.ts#drawnMode.

ontology.note: Map presentation plan and MapView activity are implemented; broader map artifact and cartographic contracts remain open. 0.11.0 declared fw:MapSpecification and the fifteen encoding properties here. That was wrong: emits records what the module named in implementation.definition asserts, and this widget is defined in src/core.ts#TYPES, which asserts nothing. The encoding terms are asserted by src/map-communication.ts and are gated by validate:ontology-coupling, which holds at zero undeclared. A release file is immutable, so 0.11.0 keeps the over-declaration and this one corrects it.

changes.description:
A MAP DRAWS EVERY LAYER IT IS GIVEN, including when polygons are among them. The ports stopped depending on a mode on 2026-10-14; the VALUE did not. `drawnMode` still picked one winner and the branch that won built the value alone, so a map wired to a study area, a point layer and a polygon layer drew the polygons and discarded the other two -- while the Sources line beneath it, built from the edges, named all three. The practitioner, 2026-10-28: "workflow shows much more connected but did not show up as layers." This is the fourth layer lost the same way: the study area on 2026-10-20, the facilities on 2026-10-22, the raster on 2026-10-23, each patched one layer at a time. The polygons branch now composes as the raster branch learned to, building the spatial map from the wired area and every point layer beside it and joining the polygons to it as a layer. One receipt still, with the map's facts appended to the polygon presentation's rather than replacing them.

A NAMED LAYER IS CATEGORICAL AND IS ITS OWN KEY. Every valueless polygon took one hard-coded `#1f77b4` on the interactive map, so the Thames above and below Teddington Lock -- the one distinction that example exists to draw -- arrived as a single blue shape over a blue river; the static plot used YlGnBu, a SEQUENTIAL ramp whose design is that a reader can rank the classes, over two categories that have no rank. Bands carrying `minutes` keep the ordered palette; named regions take Okabe-Ito, and only while the hues stay distinct -- past the palette's length there is no categorical figure to draw and the neutral wash is kept, because a repeated hue over 33 sub-districts reads as a grouping nobody asserted. The legend is built from those same names and hues. Its fallback named a modelled catchment, observations and sites over a figure drawing none of them, which is the THIRD report of a stale key on this widget -- twice fixed for the case in front of it and twice left to catch the next case wrongly.

Takes a `ground` layer: a georeferenced image drawn under everything the workflow produced. Additive and backward-compatible -- a map with nothing on that port draws exactly as before. The port type is separate from `raster` on purpose: a raster carries measurements and exists to be clipped and sampled, and ground carries a picture, so the two must not be interchangeable at a connector. See docs/experiments/143-a-georeferenced-plate-as-ground.md.

evidence.note: Repository regression coverage exists; this release entry does not certify a widget independently.
